sentences.text:
Prosecution case, in brief, is that during the period w.e.f.28/5/2018 to 1/6/2023 the applicant,
who was working as Assistant Grade-III in Block Education Office, Bhind and was assigned the duties of Creator, in connivance with co-accused persons, namely, P.S. Chauhan, S.K. Gautam, K.
Tayal, Anjan Kishor Bajpai and Avinash Singh Bhadauriya, who were also working thereat as DDO/Creator/Approver/Accountant, by misusing their unique code made excess payments to the retired/dead/on deputation/transferred employees as regards their salary and allowances, viz. HRA etc., as well as fraudulently transferred huge amount in the accounts of their family members by making false and fabricated entries in the online software and as such, misappropriated huge amount of more than Rs.1,12,37,836/- causing loss to the Government exchequer.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that it has been alleged against the applicant that he being posted as Assistant Grade-III prepared two bills amounting to Rs.39,625/- and Rs.30,331/-
vide voucher No.0361 dated 13/2/2020 in the name of Archana and Ramavtar Tripathi as Creator,
which were deposited thereafter in their accounts.

He submits that as per prosecution case itself,
both the above persons, namely, Archana and Ramavtar Tripathi are the close relatives of co-accused Anjan Kishore Vajpai, who was Accountant at the relevant period of time.
He further submits that the aforesaid bills were prepared by the co-accused Anjan Kishore Vajpai himself using the user ID & password of the applicant.

It has nowhere been alleged that any amount was transferred in the account of the applicant or his any of the relatives, which itself supports the aforesaid fact that both the above bills were prepared by the co-accused Anjan Kishore Vajpai and not by the applicant.
Applicant has falsely been implicated in the matter.
There is nothing else on record to suggest his involvement in the crime, therefore, the applicant is entitled for anticipatory bail.

5. Learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the application and submits that as per inspection report, applicant was very well posted as Assistant Grade-III at the relevant period of time and he was the Creator of the bills amounting to Rs.39,625/- and Rs.30,331/-, voucher No.0361 dated 13/2/2020.

Matter relates to embezzlement of huge public money, therefore,
requirement of applicant's custodial interrogation cannot be denied.
Hence, he is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

6. Heard the learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.
7.

Having considered the rival submissions, material produced on record and the fact that bills relating to some of the embezzled amount transferred into the accounts of co-accused persons were created by using the user ID & password of the applicant, requirement of applicant's custodial interrogation cannot be denied, hence, in view of this Court, applicant does not deserve to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the application is dismissed.
7.1 Certified copy as per Rules.

(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE Arun*
